name: Bin Hu
title: Assistant Professor; Networked Autonomous and Intelligent Learning Lab director
department: Department of Engineering Technology; Electrical and Computer Engineering affiliation
fitReason: Strong bridge between safe-learning algorithms, embedded perception and current physical multi-robot/aerial systems; especially suitable for control-aware neural models and resource-constrained autonomy.

physicalEvidence.summary: Coauthors July 2026 Neural-ESO with his current PhD student Richie Suganda: a learned disturbance predictor plus corrective observer executes actual ModalAI Seeker landing and near-ground maneuvers, using OptiTrack and 50 Hz offboard control. His current lab inventory independently lists three Seeker drones, ROSbot Pro platforms, a Jackal and motion capture; the lab demonstration page describes real two-ROSbot learned-perception/CBF leader following. March 2026 formation-aware conformal perception is explicitly Gazebo simulation and is not counted as new physical validation. The LLM-drone description includes hardware-in-the-loop testing, so it is not used to claim a separately verified autonomous foundation-model flight experiment.

shortVisit.summary: The homepage advertises student openings and the team page invites general research inquiries. Neither establishes external short-term visiting-master’s eligibility or an eight-week summer place. The current roster contains PhD students and prior local master’s advisees.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct safe neural-control and embedded robot perception methods rather than generic AI adjacency.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual learned drone experiment with current advisee plus an independently verified current lab inventory of that platform and real ROSbot demonstrations.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: General student recruitment lacks an explicit external visitor/intern pathway; no short-visit credit.
scoreReasons.freshness: July 2026 primary flight paper and lab pages updated September 28, 2026; official appointment verified.
